status: Overlay rectangles/visibility, surface descriptors/creation errors and HAL exclusive-exit loss implemented; all applicable Wine conformance still incomplete.
changes: An overlay without a current or supplied destination returns INVALIDPARAMS on initial SHOW/HIDE. Existing destination fallback for initialized hide/refresh remains. A missing destination rectangle uses the full current target, resetting its origin instead of retaining a prior rectangle. Hidden overlay position returns OVERLAYNOTVISIBLE and zeros both coordinates. Destination references, invalid rectangles, foreign owners and transport failures are covered separately.

Legacy1/2/3/4 GetSurfaceDesc thunks clear the input-only LPSURFACE flag and pointer without changing the retained descriptor used by Lock. Modern7 already does this. A description returned by a getter therefore cannot be reapplied without an explicit supplied pointer; original INVALIDPARAMS error priority is restored.

SetSurfaceDesc ignores caps2 while rejecting nonzero dwCaps and reserved caps3/4. Independent XP observations disproved the broader draft assumption that all tail fields are ignored; candidate frozen only after matching the native distinction. Native source, outputs and both environment executions remain retained.

Borrowed memory cannot back a complex mip/cube graph, including an explicit mip count of one; return INVALIDCAPS before allocation. A noncomplex one-level mip surface remains legal. A nonflipping complex cube texture with BACKBUFFERCOUNT returns INVALIDPARAMS; ordinary nonflipping surfaces retain INVALIDCAPS.

Successful newer (2/3/4/7) HAL/default EXCLUSIVE-to-NORMAL transitions without FULLSCREEN mark video allocations lost; retaining FULLSCREEN preserves them, and clearing it later from nonexclusive mode does not create another exclusive exit. This holds even when the private native HEL control surface stays valid. System and managed allocations survive, failed transitions roll back, and explicit emulation factory exit retains its native control policy. DirectDraw1 preserves allocations on exit, keyed by the invoked API view rather than object creation. Entry into exclusive keeps the previous behavior. This follows the original HAL lost_device expectations; native HEL availability is not used to waive them.
